A type I region can be written as

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,a\le x\le b,\,g(x)\le y\le f(x)\},
$$

where $f$ and $g$ are continuous functions.

To express the given region as a type I region, we first rewrite all of the given curves as functions of $x:$

$$
x=y+1\,⟹\,y=x-1
$$

The function $y=\frac{1}{2}(x-1)^{2}$ is already written as a function of $x.$

Notice that the region lies between the vertical lines $x=1$ and $x=3.$ So, we have $1\le x\le 3.$

We draw a vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower function $g(x)$ and the upper function $f(x).$ A vertical line should intersect the region in a single interval only for it to be a type I region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14096470/assets/15f9c5d526747b80766a8a3250fa2e705d5d7d9561c52e08492b7a18f1483eb6.png)

The vertical line enters the region through the lower function $y=\frac{1}{2}(x-1)^{2}$ and leaves through the upper function $y=x-1.$ So, we have $\frac{1}{2}(x-1)^{2}\le y\le x-1.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 3,\,\frac{1}{2}(x-1)^{2}\le y\le x-1\}.
$$
